Based on the search results, here's how to register multiple attendees for a Pheedloop event:

**Group Registration (One Person Buying for Multiple People):**

If the event organizer has enabled group registration, one person can purchase tickets for multiple attendees. Here's how it works:

1. During registration, select the number of tickets you want to purchase
2. You'll need to provide unique information for each attendee, including:
   - First name
   - Last name  
   - Email address (must be unique for each person)
3. Complete the payment for all tickets in one transaction

**Important notes:**
- Each attendee must have a unique email address
- The purchaser will appear in the registration records, but all ticket holders will appear in the attendees list
- Both the purchaser and all attendees they registered will receive access to the event
- This option is only available if the event organizer has configured "Ticketed (Group)" registration for that event

**Individual Registration:**
If group registration isn't enabled, each person must register separately for the event using their own email address.

The availability of group registration depends entirely on how the event organizer has set up their registration categories, so if you're unsure, check the registration page or contact the event organizer directly.

Currently, PheedLoop does not support custom registration categories. Categories do not affect functionality directly, but they do allow you to create separate registration flows. The built-in categories are Attendee, Speaker, Sponsor, and Exhibitor. You do have the option to sub-categorize ...

If you registered on PheedLoop and bought a ticket for yourself and a colleague, only you would show up in the registration section of PheedLoop. This makes sense because you are the one that created that financial transaction. On the other hand, you and your colleague will both show up in the attendees section of PheedLoop. Additionally, anyone who has been added or accepted as a speaker/exhibitor/sponsor will show up in the attendees section of PheedLoop. Currently, PheedLoop does not support custom registration categories. Categories do not affect functionality directly, but they do allow you to create separate registration flows. The built-in categories are Attendee, Speaker, Sponsor, and Exhibitor. You do have the option to sub-categorize tickets within one of the built-in categories, by creating and assigning sub-categories within a ticket's editing area found under the Registration module in your dashboard.

There are a few ways to do this, depending on what you want attendees to see once registration is complete: Change all your tickets to de-activated (hides all tickets) Set end dates on all your tickets which correspond to the end date for your registration overall (shows them, but makes them inaccessible) Hide the website page entirely under the Event Website module in your dashboard (keep in mind that you'll want to de-activate tickets as well because hiding a page does not make it inaccessible directly) Seeing a lot of in progress registrations or orders can seem concerning at first glance, but it's actually hugely beneficial. A big goal of PheedLoop as a platform is to help you more intelligently plan and execute events. Many registration systems don't capture what we call buyer intent (i.e. the intention of people wanting to do something, for example registering for your event).

However, if your accounting requirements demand an export of your finanial information on a per Ticket level, there is a way to achieve this by simply restricting the number of Tickets a registrant can purchase in any given Order to one. This way, there will always be a precise, one-to-one relationship between an individual Ticket being purchaed and the individual financial record it creates. You can make this adjustment in an individual Ticket's settings, and the global Registration settings for your event.
